guides.title: Bind FastDB into requests with exact write recovery
guides.summary: Create one FastDB binding per isolate or process with a durable pending-write store, explicit work limits and engine preflight; reads are fresh snapshots and each write is one atomic batch.
guides.markdown:
`createFastDB({ url, token, pending })` connects to a local `fastdb serve` URL (`http://127.0.0.1:4321`) or a FastDB Cloud database URL. The token is a server-only secret: a local service token or a Cloud database grant with `query` scope. The client uses Web APIs only (fetch, crypto, AbortSignal), so the same code runs on Cloudflare Workers without `nodejs_compat` and on Node.js.

Every write is saved in the pending store before dispatch. Use `FilePendingWriteStore` from `@cossackframework/fastdb/node` on Node and `DurableObjectPendingWriteStore` with the exported `FastDBPendingWrites` Durable Object on Workers; `MemoryPendingWriteStore` is for tests. When a response is lost after dispatch, `write()` throws `UncertainWriteError` and keeps the saved request. `recoverPending()` replays the exact request ID and body from a scheduled path; it never sends a replacement write. A write outside the 64-request receipt window needs a reconciler for its `kind`.

Reads use `/read` with `afterSequence` as a causal lower bound. Each call sends explicit `workLimits` (defaults from the binding). Responses with 503 or 429 and `retry-after` are retried a bounded number of times. `preflight()` reads the engine release and throws `EngineVersionError` for engines older than 2.8.0; local services are checked at connect. Request paths never warm a Cloud database: call `warm()` from a schedule. `retryConflicts` re-runs a batch the engine rolled back for a concurrent write to the same rows, only where re-evaluating the statements is correct.

guides.title: Keep FastDB values typed across JSON boundaries
guides.summary: Integers are bigint, explicit floats are Float64, record IDs keep string or integer keys, and the transport codec carries them through SSR, RPC and plugin boundaries.
guides.markdown:
FastDB results are positional rows of typed values. Integer columns decode to `bigint`, numbers to `Float64` so an integral float stays a float, and record IDs to `RecordId`, where `posts:1` with a string key differs from `posts:1` with an integer key. `Vector` and `Uint8Array` carry vectors and bytes. Pass JavaScript numbers for integers within the safe range; use `bigint` or `Float64` otherwise. `undefined`, array holes, non-finite numbers and nesting deeper than 64 are rejected.

`objects(result)` maps rows to objects by column name and throws `DuplicateColumnError` when a query repeats a column: alias duplicates instead of losing one. `one()` and `scalar()` assert cardinality.

JSON drops these types. `toTransport(value)` returns a JSON-safe, versioned form (`{ $fdb: 1, t, v }` for bigint, Float64, records, bytes and vectors; plain objects that contain `$fdb` are wrapped), and `fromTransport()` validates and restores it. `@cossackframework/fastdb/values` is the client-safe entry: it has no client, credentials or Node APIs, so components can decode values the server sent.

guides.title: Run the portable SQL ledgers on FastDB
guides.summary: sqlDatabase() gives FastDB relational tables D1's prepare().bind() shape, so core's job and notification ledgers keep their lease and fencing semantics.
guides.markdown:
The job and notification ledgers in `@cossackframework/core` (`createSqlJobStore`, `createSqlNotificationStore`) take any database with D1's `prepare(sql).bind(...).first/all/run` shape; `createD1JobStore` is the same ledger on a D1 binding. `sqlDatabase(db)` provides that shape over FastDB: SELECT and WITH statements are fresh reads, other statements are one atomic write each, `run()` reports the affected count, and positional `?` placeholders become named parameters. Integer results within the safe range become numbers, as D1 returns them.

Create the tables first with the ledger's schema (`jobStateSchema`, `notificationStateSchema`). The CMS host creates them in its host migration. Rolled-back write conflicts are retried, which keeps conditional claims equivalent to serial execution.
